articleTitle: IEE Colloquium on 'Technological Progress in Cardiology' (Digest No.19)
publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Technological Progress in Cardiology
IEE Colloquium on Technological Progress in Cardiology
abstract: The author has searched for a method which would yield a more continuous view of the possible changes in autonomic function throughout the day. Tape recordings of ECG's from normal subjects and diabetic patients with known autonomic dysfunction of varying degrees have been processed to provide many chart recordings of long sequences of analogue RR interval vs. time. Attempts to find a quantitative measure which would best reflect the degree of automatic dysfunction culminated in the realisation that the best discriminator was the rate of occurrence of 'larger jumps in RR interval from one beat to the next'. The RR interval analysis system designed using these findings is described.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Technological Progress in Cardiology
abstract: The application of bio-engineering in acute cardiac events has been significant during the last two decades. The next era of home-based medical diagnosis and treatment will require an even greater dependence on supportive bio-engineering systems. The design and development of such instrumentation will require close liaison between the physician and engineer to ensure that the patient's treatment is not compromised by not being hospitalised. This support should greatly extend the application of emergency medicine while allowing faster recovery under controlled conditions in the home environment. The dependence of such procedures will increasingly need reliable communication and hardware devices, and an infrastructure designed to extend optimal initial patient care.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Numerical modelling of the electrical activity of the cardiac conducting system
publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Technological Progress in Cardiology
abstract: The work described outlines the development of models of the HPS (His-Purkinje system) that allow body surface potentials to be calculated. This enables a much greater insight into the features of recorded waveforms by relating these to the simulated waveforms and the different sections of the HPS model.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: A novel approach to ECG signal averaging in exercise testing
publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Technological Progress in Cardiology
abstract: The use of different algorithms to achieve low noise representative beats, free of distortion caused by the processing, is discussed. The algorithms which helped the authors achieve improved ECG analysis in exercise testing, are illustrated.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Technological Progress in Cardiology
abstract: The prototype described provides a means of real time display and analysis of the ST segment in a 12-lead ECG. By displaying the signal averaged P-QRS-T complexes for the 12-lead as a static image over a 10 second period the large amount of information contained in the display can be fairly readily assessed. Since the ST segment changes which occur during myocardial ischaemia evolve over a period of minutes rather than on a beat to beat basis, analysis of the ST segment at 10 second intervals provides an adequate basis for monitoring. By incorporating a single lead for a continuous display, the rhythm can also be monitored on a beat to beat basis. The present system is limited to data sampling at 100 Hz and the processor and data structures are all limited to 8 bits. The prototype has been successfully used to monitor patients with unstable angina, patients undergoing coronary thrombolysis and angioplasty.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Non-invasive, beat-to-beat analysis of cardiac microvolt signals
publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Technological Progress in Cardiology
abstract: The authors discuss the development of a new non-invasive technique which does not rely on averaging and is capable of detecting microvolt potentials on a beat-to-beat basis. The problem is fundamentally one of extracting the desired small signals from a noisy background. The development of such a system is described and some clinical results are presented which show how the detection of microvolt signals, such as the His-Purkinje system electrogram and ventricular late potentials, may be obtained.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: A microcomputer based heart-rate variability analysis system
publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Technological Progress in Cardiology
abstract: The analysis of heart rate variability is very important in the case of examination of patients under mental load. This is an objective method, because it does not require any feed-back or communications with the patients, and thus it does not cause an additional load resulting from examination itself. Such systems can be applied in industrial medicine tests or in the case of diabetics examinations. The author started with the conversion of a standard electrocardiogram into its digital form. Then the block of digital filters was applied for removing such phenomena as: base-line drift or 50 Hz disturbances.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>
